source_observations.observation: Three distance expressions under the same verb of running. The third has short i.
The two numeral compounds are divided at yojana. The third unit has no division after aśva.
Both numeral expressions have acute on their last syllable. The third expression bears initial acute.

source_observations.locator: Sāyaṇa on Śaunaka 6.131.3, Atharvavedasaṃhitā vol. II, pp. 277–278
source_observations.observation: He reads three distances as alternatives for the person addressed, supplying a place measured by three or five yojanas or reachable by a rider. The return and fatherhood belong to subsequent clauses.
Specifically adduces aśvin and aṇ, with the place accessible to the horseman as his paraphrase.

source_observations.locator: Whitney–Lanman on AV 6.131.3, translation and Pada variants
source_observations.observation: Separates the three distances and reports differing accent and divisions of the return predicate. These differences are on a different word.
Retains final in before non-descendant aṇ. The commentary expressly contrasts another suffix and the descendant meaning.
In sentence 8 the distance is one thousand horse-days and is locative singular. Sentence 16 has seven metres for the twin gods, with short i and plural agreement.
Distinguishes the required number of recitations, the location of the heavenly world and the deity of the seven metrical groups.

source_observations.locator: Aitareya Brāhmaṇa with Sāyaṇa, printed p. 276, PDF leaf 2, main commentary and notes
source_observations.observation: Visual reading gives a strong horse travelling in one day, multiplication by a thousand, 5.2.19 by its Sanskrit wording, and an elevated deśa as referent. The footnote cites Amara 2.8.47.

source_observations.locator: Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, paragraph with the twin gods winning the race, TITUS ab129, sentences 1–4
source_observations.observation: The Aśvin recitation is named for the winners. Its locative recurs with three contributions within the liturgy.
The grammatical example specifies a hundred and an act of flying. Neither of the new primary addresses contains those two elements.
